docs/how-it-works.md:22:5. **Open the thread** ([`src/thread.ts`](../src/thread.ts)). pi-action gets `refs/pi/threads/<number>` and `refs/pi/worktrees/<number>`, opens the conversation, and restores the files that the earlier run left uncommitted (see [Working-tree continuity](threads.md#working-tree-continuity)). If an earlier run did not complete its work, pi continues that work.
docs/security.md:79:pi-action stores the full conversation in `refs/pi/threads/<number>`, also the output of tools. It stores the files that pi leaves uncommitted in `refs/pi/worktrees/<number>`, also untracked files that git does not ignore. All people who can read the repository can read these refs. Keep secrets away from the agent, as for all CI jobs. Make git ignore files with secrets, or list them in `worktree_snapshot_exclude`. See [Durable threads](threads.md#read-a-thread) and [Working-tree continuity](threads.md#working-tree-continuity).
docs/threads.md:3:Each issue or pull request is one pi conversation, a **thread**. pi-action stores the thread in your repository, as a chain of git commits on `refs/pi/threads/<number>`. Thus, a later run continues the conversation on any runner, with all that pi saw and did before.
docs/threads.md:5:pi-action stores threads with [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable). The storage code is in [`src/storage`](../src/storage). `refs/pi/threads/<number>` is a custom ref: it is not a branch, and GitHub does not show it as one.
docs/threads.md:68:pi-action stores the snapshots of issue 42 on `refs/pi/worktrees/42`, next to `refs/pi/threads/42`, and pushes the two refs together in one atomic push (`git push --atomic`). Thus, the remote never has the conversation without its snapshot.
